evidence.ran: bash .loop/verify.sh (fast shell suites + claude plugin test mods/bussin-loop-status: 52 pass, new test "waiting changes show as plain lines in 'Your changes', with when they apply and an Undo that removes the file" on terminal and desktop, running and stopped loops)

notes:
Did: loadLoop reads <loop>/.loop/inbox via fs.list (names matching ^[0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9]+\.json$, sorted, at most 50) into LoopView.changes ({name, path, line}; InboxChange in types/index.d.ts). changeLine() words each op: Add 'x', Reword 'x', Skip 'x', Run 'x' next, Approve screenshots of 'x', Fix after review: 'x' (task names from the item's plain sentence, typed text cleaned and capped at 80 characters); unreadable files and unknown ops are left out. A 'Your changes · N waiting' bordered Box sits right under the header with one row per change and an Undo button keyed undo-<file name> that runs $.process.run(['rm', '--', path]) and refreshes (a failed rm toasts why). Under it: 'Applied before the next task starts.' when canStop(snapshot) (running or queued, driver alive), else 'Applied when the loop runs next.'. sendChange now refreshes after writing, so a new change shows in the box at once, and its toast uses the same timing sentence.
Learned: openTaskAtom and openAreasAtom persist across pane mounts in one test, so pressing a task that an earlier mount left open closes it; and an area opens by itself only while it has running or failing tasks, so on a stopped loop press area-<name> first. shortTitle() cuts text at the first ': ', so it is wrong for text the user typed; changeLine uses its own 80-character cap.
Lesson: [bussin-lean] first draft passed user-typed text through shortTitle, which would show 'Search: suggests…' as 'Search'; review caught it → only use shortTitle on item descriptions, never on text the user typed.
Lesson: [tests] two gate runs failed because the test pressed a task that an earlier mount left open (atoms persist across mounts) and pressed a task in an area that was closed on a stopped loop → before pressing inside a pane in a later mount, account for the atom state earlier mounts left behind.
